summary.text: Zora Labs runs a social app for creating and trading coins and develops the software that powers those trades, according to Blockworks.
Dee Goens took over as chief executive in September 2026, he announced on X.
People can turn posts into coins, activate a profile coin for free, and use Explore to find coins to buy, Zora says.
Creator and post coins have a 1% base trading fee, and the app lists a transaction fee, according to Zora.
Profile coins trade against ZORA, and posts usually trade against their creator’s coin, the project says.
Trading software automatically collects fees and pays rewards in ZORA on Base, the project says.
Creators can choose a different asset as their coin’s trading partner and receive 0.70% of each trade, the project says.
Zora also lists a separate network that Keylo says was used for minting digital collectibles.
The Base token reports a supply of ten billion ZORA, while one section of Zora’s white paper gives one billion.

open_questions: Which wallets currently control distribution of team, investor and treasury ZORA, and how do their balances compare with the published unlock schedules?
Do the currently active coin pools enforce the published reward splits for each coin type and chain?
Which mechanism backs the Solana ZORA mint, and does it represent a bridged balance or a separate issuance?
Who currently operates Zora Network infrastructure, and which current app features rely on it?
Who holds the six signing wallets for the coin factory’s Safe?
Which contract created the coin factory proxy internally, and which authority controls that deployer?
Will Zora correct the one-billion supply figure in its August 2025 white paper?

notes: All 67 lines from F1 are carried with their origins. The Base ZORA token is main because the brief and Zora identify it as the official Base token, and Zora describes it as the pairing currency and rewards asset. Rechecked Base contract calls at block 61365201. The public Base RPC independently returned the same supply and the two deployment-boundary code readings. The February deployment, March mint and April trading and airdrop are separate events. Verified the ZORA deployment factory by deriving the token address from the successful CREATE2 transaction, with the transaction sender recorded separately. The homepage publishes the main address, but the token metadata points to theme.wtf and no stronger tie to zora.co was verified. Docs and help centre remain weak. The external official account ties were checked against Zora’s own account list and repository link. The two individual X accounts are listed with no tie. The bridge metric remains as an earlier claim, while Size uses DefiLlama’s Base coin trading volume. The Solana balance is shown separately based on Solscan and the public Solana RPC. Blockworks classifies it as a direct issuance. No cross-chain supply total is asserted. The factory owner, claim admin and claim allocation setter are distinct roles. A reverting token owner call and an empty implementation slot do not establish the absence of every token authority. The docs homepage prompt to fetch and follow another file was ignored.
